title: Eisenhower Matrix: free Android app and printable template
description: What the Eisenhower Matrix is, how to use it, a free printable template (PDF), and a private Android to-do app with no account, no ads and no subscription.
og_desc: Sort your to-do list by urgent and important. Free printable template and a private Android app.
h1: Sort your to-do list by urgent and important
lead: A free printable Eisenhower Matrix, a short guide to using it, and a private Android app that does the sorting for you.
cta_play: Get the app on Google Play
what_p: The Eisenhower Matrix is a way of deciding what to do next by asking two questions about every task: is it urgent, and is it important? The answers put the task in one of four boxes.
do_text: Deadlines today, real problems. Act on these now.
sc_text: Health, planning, learning, relationships. Give each one a date.
de_text: Interruptions and other people's deadlines. Hand off, or do quickly.
ba_text: Revisit later, or let it go.
history_p: It is named after Dwight D. Eisenhower, who is credited with the line "What is important is seldom urgent and what is urgent is seldom important." Stephen Covey later made the four boxes popular in The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People.
howto_h2: How to use it in five minutes
s1t: Empty your head onto one list before sorting anything.
s2t: Important means it moves something you care about. Urgency is easier to feel, so judge it second.
s3t: Urgent means there is a real cost if it is not done soon.
s4b: Give every Schedule task a date.
s4t: This box holds what matters most and it never shouts. Without a date it does not get done.
s5t: For each overdue task decide: done, today, another day, or drop it.
mistake_t: putting almost everything in Do. If more than a handful of tasks are both urgent and important, some of them are only urgent. Ask who set the deadline.
tpl_p: One page, four boxes, room to write. Print it, or keep it on your desk as a daily sheet.
tpl_free: Free for personal and classroom use. No email needed.
app_p: Eisenhower Matrix: To-Do List does the sorting for you. Mark a task as urgent, important, or both, and it lands in the right box.

q4: What is the difference between urgent and important?
a4: Urgent tasks have a real cost if they are not done soon. Important tasks move something you care about. Many tasks are one without the other, which is the whole point of the matrix.
q5: What should go in the fourth box?
a5: Tasks that are neither urgent nor important. Some people call the box Delete or Eliminate. The app calls it Backlog, because many of these are worth a second look before they are dropped.
